weather.tip: 84% chance of rain through the evening under overcast skies — carry an umbrella for the commute home and give yourself extra time near underpasses and low-lying stretches that pool up fast.

around.headline: Missing Bengaluru techie feared dead: drone spots body-like object on Shivagange
around.summary: The techie who set off alone up Shivagange on Monday, weeks from his wedding, is still missing, and a search drone has now spotted what may be a body on the hill; reports say his phone history included searches for suicide locations. Always share your route and expected return time with someone before a solo trek, and check in when you're back.
around.source: The Times of India, NDTV, India Today

around.headline: Karnataka Bandh called for August 13: banks, buses, schools and metro likely hit
around.summary: A statewide bandh backed by Vatal Nagraj's andolan is set for tomorrow, with banks, buses, schools and metro services expected to be disrupted in Bengaluru. Plan errands and travel for today or push them past tomorrow, and keep cash on hand in case ATMs and branches are shut.

around.headline: FDA crackdown widens: Zepto warehouse sealed, hygiene lapses found at Zomato Hyperpure too
around.summary: After sealing a Zepto dark-store warehouse over 'extremely unhygienic' conditions, inspectors also flagged labelling and storage lapses at a Zomato Hyperpure unit, even as expired food and cockroaches turned up at the health department's own Vidhana Soudha canteen. If you order in from either platform this week, check the order for anything off before eating and report issues through the app.

around.headline: Karnataka bans sale and manufacture of gutkha and pan masala for a year
around.summary: The state government has prohibited the sale, storage and manufacture of gutkha, pan masala and some other tobacco products for the next 12 months. Shops caught stocking banned items can be fined or shut down, so don't be surprised if your usual paan shop stops carrying them.
around.source: The Times of India, The Indian Express

around.headline: Prakash Raj's voter-roll deletion claim disputed by Bengaluru's civic body
around.summary: After actor Prakash Raj said his name had vanished from the electoral rolls during the SIR exercise, the BJP and the civic body countered that his entry wasn't deleted — records show he'd shifted address. If you flagged an issue with your own name during SIR, verify on the Karnataka CEO website before assuming it's an error rather than an address mismatch.

around.headline: CAG flags Bengaluru Metro planning failures: ₹6,600 crore cost overrun, ridership below target
around.summary: A CAG report says Namma Metro's Phase 1 and 2 land acquisition costs overshot by roughly ₹6,600 crore while ridership came in well below projections, even as the network posted its highest-ever daily ridership this week. Worth watching if you rely on future metro phases — planning slippage like this tends to mean delayed timelines.
around.source: Swarajya, The Indian Express, The Hindu

around.headline: Mumbai landslide kills 6, rescuers use a victim's phone camera to search for survivors
around.summary: A landslide in Mumbai has killed six people, with rescue teams resorting to a recovered phone's camera to help locate anyone still trapped. A reminder that monsoon landslide risk isn't unique to hill towns — steep, waterlogged slopes near construction sites in any city can give way fast.

street_smart.title: You've ordered from a food-delivery dark-store whose warehouse the FDA just sealed for unhygienic conditions. You post a public complaint online, and within minutes someone claiming to be from 'FSSAI support' DMs you offering to fast-track a refund. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident today: FDA inspectors sealed a Zepto dark-store warehouse over 'extremely unhygienic' conditions and flagged labelling/storage lapses at a Zomato Hyperpure unit in Bengaluru (The Times of India, NDTV).
street_smart.situation: After hearing the news, you check your recent orders and realise you ordered from the flagged warehouse twice this month. You post a complaint tagging the platform. Minutes later, an account claiming to be 'FSSAI Grievance Support' DMs you, says they can expedite your refund and compensation, and asks you to pay a small 'verification fee' via UPI along with your bank details to process it.

choices.text: Pay the small 'verification fee' by UPI and share your bank details, since it seems like a fast way to get compensated.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. No government agency or platform grievance desk ever asks for a fee to 'process' a refund, and no legitimate refund requires your bank login details. Accounts that slide into your replies after a public complaint, offering to 'help' for a payment, are a scam pattern that's grown alongside social-media customer service.

choices.text: Post an angry follow-up review and move on — you've said your piece.
choices.feedback: Risky. A public post might get attention, but it creates no official record and nothing obliges the platform or FSSAI to act on it. It also leaves you exposed to exactly the kind of fake 'support' DM described above, since scammers monitor public complaints for targets.

choices.text: Call the platform's in-app customer care, ask for a refund, and consider the matter closed once you get one.
choices.feedback: Risky. A refund from the platform fixes your money but doesn't create a record with the food safety regulator, so the underlying hygiene issue at that warehouse goes unreported to anyone who can actually inspect and act on it.

choices.text: File a complaint with your order details and photos via the FSSAI Food Safety Voice app or the National Consumer Helpline (1915), ignoring any DM offering to 'help' for a fee.
choices.feedback: Correct. Filing through FSSAI's official channel or the National Consumer Helpline creates a trackable, official complaint that can trigger real inspection or enforcement action — and it costs nothing. Legitimate grievance redressal never starts with someone DMing you asking for payment first.

takeaways: No genuine support agency or company DMs you first asking for a fee or your bank details to 'process' a complaint you posted publicly — that pattern is always a scam.
For food safety issues, use the FSSAI Food Safety Voice app or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 — both create an official record that can lead to real action, and both are free.

Before ordering from a platform or outlet in the news for a hygiene lapse, check if it's been cleared by a follow-up inspection, and keep your order receipt in case you need to file a complaint later.

quiz.question: What is expected to be disrupted in Bengaluru by the Karnataka Bandh called for August 13?
options: Banks, buses, schools and metro services
Nothing — the bandh was called off
quiz.why: The bandh is backed by Vatal Nagraj's andolan; statewide bandhs in Karnataka typically see transport unions and trade bodies participate, though enforcement and compliance can vary by area.

quiz.question: After actor Prakash Raj said his name was deleted from Bengaluru's voter rolls, what did the civic body and BJP say in response?
options: His entry wasn't deleted — records show he had shifted address
They admitted an error and reinstated his name immediately
They confirmed the deletion was intentional
They said no voter roll revision was underway
quiz.why: This is playing out during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls — anyone can check their own entry on the Karnataka CEO's website rather than relying on hearsay.

quiz.question: A landslide in Mumbai this week killed how many people, with rescuers using a victim's phone camera to search for survivors?
quiz.why: Monsoon landslide risk applies to any city with steep, waterlogged slopes near construction or hillside settlements — not just traditional hill stations.

quiz.question: Roughly how high above sea level does Bengaluru sit?
quiz.why: That elevation (~920 m) is a big reason Bengaluru's climate stays milder than most Indian cities at similar latitudes.

quiz.question: What is the RBI's 'repo rate'?
options: The rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
The tax rate on repossessed property
The interest rate banks pay depositors on savings accounts
quiz.why: When the RBI cuts the repo rate, banks' own borrowing costs fall, which usually (with a lag) shows up as cheaper home and auto loans.
